factual_methodology.summary: Read and checked the historical, laboratory and official institutional source record: 2003 Fog of War and CNA 2014 on Vietnam measurement; 2012/2014 Facebook interventions; 2023 chronological feed; 2025 meta-analysis; 2026 preliminary DSA finding. All major claims distinguish causal experiment, observational relationship, institutional finding and historical interpretation.

research_depth.summary: Reviewed EN 70,908 characters, PT-BR 75,128 characters; 24 substantive chapters and full bibliography per language. Covers quantified administration, technical ranking, platform economy, youth psychology, aura, Brazilian politics, France, Ukraine, automated work, Thiel, regulation, counter-hypotheses and falsifiable futures.

evidence_traceability.summary: 24 numbered references in both languages, 24/24 labels declared and used, including original academic and institutional publications from Nature, PNAS, Science, Psychological Bulletin, CNA, OECD, Senate France, the European Commission, Brazilian researchers and agencies. All high-impact platform count and sample denominators are stated and qualified.

counterfactual_review.summary: Directly compares confirmed and absent evidence: association is not an induced brain injury; selected pro-Bolsonaro WhatsApp samples do not establish election causation; French platform mentions do not sum to 100% and cannot be construed as population share; Ukraine videos do not prove enlistment; experiments demonstrate limited and inconsistent attitude responses.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: The two quantitative chart series, 108/24/1 and 36/5/4/2/2/1/0.6, match exactly between languages with original-source denominators, dates and qualifications. Two detailed evidence tables, a two-chain causal flow, a case-study regional map and two local original SVG illustrations per locale; matching image paths and CC BY 4.0 author credits verified.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Corporate, legal, neurological, military and political factual claims attributed and separated from causal theories; substantive reporting has no conversational scaffolding, internal pipeline notes or unverified synthetic historical photographs. Bilingual version preserves 24-section logic, sources and empirical status, not just summaries.

source_vintage_and_context.summary: Differentiates 2018 WhatsApp/Facebook/YouTube election dynamics from 2022 TikTok/Kwai content supply, 2023 French/Brazilian events, 2025 short-video literature, 2026 Brazilian ECA Digital entry into force and European Commission preliminary allegations.

source_integrity.summary: Bilingual staged manuscripts and the pending v2 snapshot reread and tied to exact Git SHA values; 24 numbered source identities and corresponding URLs inspected; two original SVG assets present at referenced repository paths.

contrary_evidence: Randomised experiments demonstrate some social or expressive influence, while the 2023 chronological-feed intervention found no significant short-run changes in key political attitudes despite large exposure changes.

Bolsonarism developed amid economic, institutional and cultural disputes that predated the observed network communications. Neither WhatsApp content counts nor a sample of videos can establish vote shares attributable to algorithms.
Digital recording may document harm, provide civic accountability or foster community. Aura farming is an example of often playful non-violent offline social participation.
Short-video use and poorer attention indicators are associated in synthesised studies; selection effects, reverse causality, duration and subgroup differences limit causal extrapolation.
limitations: Some references are research abstracts, government disclosures or journalistic investigations rather than full experimental replication; not all external URLs were independently tested for uptime.
Platform ranking weights and intervention mechanisms are proprietary; historical user-count experiments do not establish today's universal platform behaviour.
The French inspectorate sample rates are non-exhaustive and the Brazil sample refers to high-interaction content in selected groups; the figures cannot be treated as nationally representative.
The manuscript does not claim proof of platform-induced military enlistment or violent action, and it does not diagnose any individual or age group.
Two source-localised inline illustrations and one optional original cover are editorial art, not independent photographic evidence.
Full site deployment remains separate from editorial approval and requires a successful GitHub Actions build and configured hosting credentials.
notes: Evidence-based editorial verification performed after the producer completed both manuscripts, with source identity, terminology, political neutrality, numerical parity, format, images and exact SHAs checked; the public publisher must independently repeat immutable-hash and registry-ledger checks before promoting.

en.title: The Algorithmic Revolution: From the Quantification of War to the Struggle over Attention, Behaviour and Power
en.deck: A long historical and empirical inquiry into algorithmic power: McNamara and the limits of quantification, recommender systems and attention markets, psychology and short videos, digital political mobilisation in Brazil, French unrest, Ukraine's war imagery, automated work decisions, Peter Thiel and the governance of AI.
en.regime: Quantitative systems increasingly mediate attention, identity, work and social coordination, without a proven general law of behavioural control.
en.key_risk: Mistaking algorithmic exposure for causation, aesthetic similarity for a common motive, or statistical association for forced behavioural change.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: Research documented through 2 November 2026 BRT; publication date 3 November 2026. Distinguishes 2010/2012 and 2014 experiments, 2018/2022 Brazilian evidence, 2023 French unrest, 2025 meta-analysis, and preliminary 2026 regulation.
producer_checks.editorial_novelty: Systematic genealogy from quantitative state administration and McNamara's Vietnam-era measures to contemporary feedback loops, identity performance, filmed conflict, political mobilisation, algorithmic management and the economics of attention.
producer_checks.research_depth: English about 9,632 words / 70,908 characters, PT-BR about 10,074 words / 75,128 characters. Exactly 24 substantive chapters plus a full references section; includes causal models, competing hypotheses and falsification criteria.
producer_checks.source_check: 24 numbered academic, historical, institutional, governmental and documented journalistic references present and cited in both editions; primary empirical numbers trace to CNA, Nature, PNAS, Science, Psychological Bulletin, Piaia/Alves, Agência Pública/UFMG, InternetLab, Sénat, OECD and European Commission.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Both editions have two quantitative charts (TikTok/Kwai provenance: 108/24/1; French inspectorate sample rates: 36/5/4/2/2/1/0.6), two evidence tables, one causal flow, one geographic case map and two localized original SVG inline illustrations. Original cover illustration reserved for the public media registry after QA.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: 25 matching H2 headings including references, 24/24 numbered source entries with identical URLs, identical chart numeric data and image paths, logically aligned evidence and counterarguments. Both versions use the same report slug and media provenance.
producer_checks.psychological_integrity: Avoids 'dopamine depletion' myths, distinguishes correlations and clinical harm, treats aura farming as often playful and nonviolent, limits conclusions about violence and enlistment to documented evidence.
producer_checks.political_neutrality: Bolsonarism case distinguishes 2018 WhatsApp/YouTube/Facebook from later short-form video platforms, pre-existing preferences and crises from media mechanisms, strategic amplification from genuine political support, and digital speech from unlawful action.
producer_checks.security_integrity: The Ukraine and French cases distinguish verified events, selected audiovisual samples, legal context, platform documentation and unproven recruitment/violent conduct causal theories.
limitations: Most platform ranking weights are proprietary; public statements cannot independently establish operating optimisation.
French platform percentages are limited to inspectorate sample references; they do not sum to 100 and are not national platform market shares.
Brazilian message counts and short-video provenance originate in bounded samples; the article does not estimate election vote causation.
The 2025 short-video meta-analysis reports correlational synthesis, not experimental proof of permanent cognitive injury.
Some third-party works are cited only, not reproduced; three illustrations are original conceptual art and never presented as event photography.

publication.revision_reason: First full historical, political-economic and sociopsychological research on algorithmic governance and attention power, connected to the accelerationism programme but broader than any one political movement.
